_meta.name: default-separation-ruleset
_meta.description: Machine-readable separation-of-concerns policy for AI agent infrastructure. The Separation Enforcer checks an infrastructure config against these rules and exits non-zero if any blocking rule is violated. Designed to run in CI before an agent is deployed.
_meta.philosophy: Each rule states one thing that must be true. A rule has an 'enforce' level: 'block' fails the check, 'warn' reports but passes. Teams can copy this file, tighten or relax levels, and version it alongside their infrastructure.

rules.name: Production data and backups must not share a volume
rules.rationale: Co-located backups share the fate of the data they protect. One destructive call ends both. This is the PocketOS failure.
rules.remediation: Place backups on a distinct volume in a separate account or project.

rules.name: Production data and backups must not share an account
rules.rationale: Account-level isolation is the standard last line of defence for backups.
rules.remediation: Use a dedicated backup account with its own credentials, unreachable by the agent.

rules.name: No credential may hold both production and staging access
rules.rationale: Environment-spanning credentials let a staging task reach production by mistake.

rules.name: An agent's default credential must not hold destructive capability
rules.rationale: The credential an agent uses for routine work should never be able to cause irreversible loss. Destructive capability belongs in a separate, deliberately-loaded credential.
rules.remediation: Move destructive capability to a single-purpose credential loaded only for the specific step that needs it.

rules.name: No credential may have destructive capability at account-wide scope
rules.rationale: Destructive power plus unlimited scope is the maximum blast radius configuration.
rules.remediation: Scope any destructive credential to a single project or resource.

rules.name: Read access and destructive access should not share a credential
rules.rationale: Bundling routine reads with destruction means every read step carries unused destructive potential.
rules.remediation: Split into a default read-only credential and a separate destructive credential.

rules.name: Every production resource should declare a backup counterpart
rules.rationale: A production resource with no backup declared in the config is either unprotected or undocumented. Both are problems.
rules.remediation: Declare the backup resource in the config, or create one if it does not exist.
